entries.claim: `phaseDirsIn` follows symlinks for both `_archive-*` groups and their phase entries, so the new replay locator is not confined to the planning root.
entries.failure_scenario: An untrusted project can create `.planning/_archive-x` as a symlink to an arbitrary readable directory, or `.planning/phases/1` as such a symlink. `entriesIn(dir)` and then `planFilesIn(join(dir, name))` follow it; replay subsequently calls `declaredFilesIn` on the external directory and scans the files its PLAN declares. Thus `route.mjs replay --file <project>/.planning/config.json` can be induced to read and process PLAN data outside the selected project rather than only `phases/` and archive directories beneath its planning root. Reject symlinks/non-directories with `lstat` and enforce that resolved paths remain below `planningRoot`.

entries.claim: The archive-aware locator has no bound on directory entries, archive groups, phase directories, or conforming plans, allowing an untrusted planning tree to cause unbounded synchronous reads and memory use.
entries.failure_scenario: A repository can contain thousands of `_archive-*` directories, each with thousands of child names containing `PLAN.md`. `phaseDirsIn` materializes every root/group directory with `readdirSync`, probes every child, and replay then reads every discovered plan and its declared files. There is a per-plan byte limit, but no limit on the number of directories or plans, so one replay can consume arbitrarily large CPU, memory, and I/O and hang the routing command. Apply explicit traversal/result limits (and report truncation) before walking all archive and phase entries.
